# insee.admin.data.2022

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of `insee.admin.data.2022` is to provide ready-to-use datasets for French administrative segmentation (millesime 2022), combining semantic and spatial data from INSEE at various administrative scales.

## Installation

This package is not available on CRAN. You can install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
remotes::install_github("AcidyBee/insee.admin.data.2022")
```

## Datasets

| Dataset | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `insee_admin_decoupage` | Hierarchical links between administrative levels (region, department, commune, etc.) |
| `insee_admin_spatial` | Spatial data (`sf` objects) for each administrative level |
| `lut_code_label` | Lookup table between administrative codes and their labels |

## Raw data

In addition to the processed datasets, the package ships raw INSEE files in `inst/extdata/`. These files can be accessed with `system.file()` and can be used as `sf` objects.

```{r raw-data, eval = FALSE}
path_to_extdata <- system.file("extdata", package = "insee.admin.data.2022")
list.files(path_to_extdata)
```

## Source

Raw INSEE files are shipped in `inst/extdata/`. The processed datasets in `data/` are generated from these files by the scripts in `data-raw/`.

## Data Compression and Size

This package contains large datasets compressed with `xz`.  
- Total installed size: ~400 Mb  
- To reduce local disk usage, load only needed datasets with `data("dataset_name", package = "insee.admin.data.2022")`.

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to load and explore the administrative data:

```{r example}
library(insee.admin.data.2022)

# Hierarchical links between administrative levels
head(insee_admin_decoupage)

# Lookup table for codes and labels
head(lut_code_label)
```

### Spatial data

Spatial data are provided as `sf` objects. Here is a quick overview of the available layers:

```{r spatial, eval = FALSE}
# Load the spatial dataset
data("insee_admin_spatial", package = "insee.admin.data.2022")

# Explore the structure
names(insee_admin_spatial)
```
